facts.text: Frogs are amphibians, which means they can live both in water and on land.
Frogs are cold-blooded, so their body temperature matches the air or water around them.
There are more than 7,700 different kinds of frogs in the world.
Frogs have been around for about 200 million years, even longer than dinosaurs.
Frogs have smooth, wet skin that helps them breathe and drink water right through it.
The smallest frog in the world is only about as big as a fingernail.
The biggest frog is the goliath frog, which can weigh as much as a newborn baby.
Frogs have big bulging eyes on top of their heads that let them see in almost every direction at once.
A frog's long, sticky tongue can snap out and catch a bug faster than you can blink.
Frogs live on every continent in the world except Antarctica.
Many frogs live near ponds, swamps, rivers, and lakes because they need water to lay their eggs.
Some frogs live high up in trees in the rainforest and never come down to the ground.
The wood frog can survive being frozen solid in winter and then thaw out and hop away in spring.
Frogs eat insects like flies, mosquitoes, and crickets.
A frog catches food with its sticky tongue in less than one second.
Frogs use their eyes to help push food down their throat when they swallow.
Baby frogs, called tadpoles, eat tiny plants called algae that grow in the water.
Frogs lay their eggs in water, and the eggs look like a squishy blob of jelly called frogspawn.
Baby frogs start out as tadpoles with long tails and no legs, and they breathe with gills like fish.
As a tadpole grows, it sprouts legs, loses its tail, and turns into a frog in a change called metamorphosis.
It can take a tadpole a few weeks to many months to finish turning into a frog.
Frogs are some of the best jumpers in the animal world and can leap more than 50 times their own body length.
Frogs have long, strong back legs that are built for jumping and swimming.
Tree frogs have sticky pads on their toes that work like suction cups to help them climb.
Some frogs called flying frogs can spread their webbed feet wide and glide through the air between trees.
Poison dart frogs are tiny and come in bright colors like red, blue, and yellow to warn other animals to stay away.
The red-eyed tree frog has bright red eyes that can startle predators and give it time to escape.
The American bullfrog is one of the biggest frogs in North America and makes a deep sound like "jug-o-rum."
The European common frog is one of the most widespread frogs and can be found in gardens, forests, and meadows.
Many frogs use camouflage, which means their colors and patterns help them blend in and hide from predators.
Male frogs croak and sing loudly to call for a mate, and each kind of frog has its own special song.
Frog populations around the world are getting smaller because of pollution and habitat loss.
Frogs help people by eating lots of mosquitoes and other pest insects.
